hello-polite.meaningNote: Standard polite greeting suitable for any time of day.

good-evening.meaningNote: Formal or polite greeting after sunset.
good-evening.exampleSentence: Good evening, we have a table reserved.

how-are-you.meaningNote: Casual and friendly check-in on someone's well-being.
how-are-you.exampleSentence: Hi Maria, how are you doing today?

nice-to-meet-you.meaningNote: Courteous phrase when introduced to someone for the first time.
nice-to-meet-you.exampleSentence: I am Carlos, nice to meet you.

thank-you-very-much.meaningNote: Expression of deep or sincere gratitude.
thank-you-very-much.exampleSentence: Thank you very much for your kind assistance.

you-are-welcome.exampleSentence: You are welcome, happy to help anytime.

please.meaningNote: Fundamental marker of politeness when requesting anything.
please.exampleSentence: Could you please pass the water?

excuse-me-pardon.meaningNote: Used to capture attention politely or to pass through a crowd.
excuse-me-pardon.exampleSentence: Excuse me, may I get past?

goodbye-take-care.meaningNote: Warm parting phrase wishing safety to the other person.
goodbye-take-care.exampleSentence: Goodbye, take care on your flight home!

a-table-for-two-please.meaningNote: Standard request when entering a restaurant.
a-table-for-two-please.exampleSentence: Good evening, a table for two inside, please.

can-i-see-the-menu.text: May I see the menu, please?
can-i-see-the-menu.meaningNote: Requesting the printed or digital food selection.
can-i-see-the-menu.exampleSentence: Excuse me, may I see the menu and drink specials?

what-do-you-recommend.meaningNote: Inquiring about house specialties or popular local delicacies.
what-do-you-recommend.exampleSentence: Everything looks tasty; what do you recommend here?

the-check-please.text: Could we have the check, please?
the-check-please.meaningNote: Signaling the server that you are ready to settle payment.
the-check-please.exampleSentence: We are all done, could we have the check, please?

i-am-allergic-to-peanuts.meaningNote: Vital health safety advisory for food preparers.
i-am-allergic-to-peanuts.exampleSentence: Please ensure there are no nuts in this; I am allergic to peanuts.

is-this-dish-spicy.meaningNote: Clarifying the chili or heat level of a meal.
is-this-dish-spicy.exampleSentence: I have a delicate stomach; is this dish spicy?

water-without-ice-please.exampleSentence: Just a glass of tap or bottled water without ice, please.

delicious-compliment.text: The food was delicious, thank you
delicious-compliment.meaningNote: Hearty praise for the cook and dining staff.
delicious-compliment.exampleSentence: Compliments to the chef, the food was delicious!

is-this-vegetarian.meaningNote: Verifying lack of meat, poultry, or seafood broth.
is-this-vegetarian.exampleSentence: Does this soup contain meat broth, or is it strictly vegetarian?

can-i-have-this-to-go.text: Can I have this to go, please?
can-i-have-this-to-go.meaningNote: Requesting a takeout box for remaining food.
can-i-have-this-to-go.exampleSentence: We could not finish our meal; can I have this to go, please?

what-is-your-name.meaningNote: Polite question when introducing yourself to someone new.
what-is-your-name.exampleSentence: Hello, my name is Alex; what is your name?

it-is-my-first-time-here.text: It is my first time visiting here.
it-is-my-first-time-here.meaningNote: Friendly icebreaker when chatting with locals.
it-is-my-first-time-here.exampleSentence: It is my first time visiting here, and the city is beautiful.

where-are-you-from.meaningNote: Common small-talk question about someone's hometown or country.
where-are-you-from.exampleSentence: We are visiting from Canada; where are you from?

is-this-your-hometown.meaningNote: Asking whether someone grew up in the current city or town.
is-this-your-hometown.exampleSentence: You know the neighborhood so well; is this your hometown?

what-do-you-do-for-a-living.text: What do you do for a living?
what-do-you-do-for-a-living.meaningNote: Polite question about someone's profession or occupation.
what-do-you-do-for-a-living.exampleSentence: I work as a teacher; what do you do for a living?

how-long-have-you-lived-here.text: How long have you lived here?
how-long-have-you-lived-here.meaningNote: Asking a resident how long they have lived in the area.
how-long-have-you-lived-here.exampleSentence: It is a wonderful neighborhood; how long have you lived here?

what-do-you-like-to-do.text: What do you like to do in your free time?
what-do-you-like-to-do.meaningNote: Asking about hobbies and personal interests.
what-do-you-like-to-do.exampleSentence: I enjoy hiking; what do you like to do in your free time?

that-is-interesting.meaningNote: Warm conversational response showing active interest.
that-is-interesting.exampleSentence: That's interesting! I did not know that about the city.

it-was-nice-talking-to-you.text: It was nice talking to you.
it-was-nice-talking-to-you.meaningNote: Polite way to wrap up a conversation before leaving.
it-was-nice-talking-to-you.exampleSentence: I have to catch my train now, but it was nice talking to you.

have-a-nice-day.exampleSentence: Thank you for your time, have a nice day!

how-much-is-this.meaningNote: Essential question when checking the price of an item.
how-much-is-this.exampleSentence: Excuse me, how much is this handmade bag?

is-this-available-in-another-size.text: Is this available in another size?
is-this-available-in-another-size.meaningNote: Asking a clerk for a larger or smaller clothing or shoe size.
is-this-available-in-another-size.exampleSentence: This shirt is a bit small; is this available in another size?

do-you-have-another-color.meaningNote: Checking whether an item comes in other colors.
do-you-have-another-color.exampleSentence: I like this style; do you have another color?

can-i-try-this-on.meaningNote: Asking permission to use the fitting room for clothing or shoes.
can-i-try-this-on.exampleSentence: Excuse me, can I try this on? Where is the fitting room?

is-there-a-discount.meaningNote: Inquiring about current promotions or cash discounts.
is-there-a-discount.exampleSentence: Is there a discount if I pay in cash?

can-you-lower-the-price.meaningNote: Used for friendly bargaining at open-air markets and souvenir stalls.
can-you-lower-the-price.exampleSentence: I would like to buy two; can you lower the price a little?

i-am-just-looking-thank-you.text: I am just looking, thank you.
i-am-just-looking-thank-you.meaningNote: Polite response to a salesperson when browsing without needing help yet.
i-am-just-looking-thank-you.exampleSentence: I am just looking right now, thank you.

where-can-i-find-this-item.text: Where can I find this item?
where-can-i-find-this-item.meaningNote: Asking store staff which aisle or section carries a product.
where-can-i-find-this-item.exampleSentence: Excuse me, where can I find this item in the store?

can-i-return-this.meaningNote: Asking about the store's return or exchange policy.
can-i-return-this.exampleSentence: If it does not fit, can I return this tomorrow with the receipt?

can-i-get-a-shopping-bag.text: Can I get a shopping bag?
can-i-get-a-shopping-bag.meaningNote: Requesting a carrier bag at checkout.
can-i-get-a-shopping-bag.exampleSentence: Can I get a shopping bag for these groceries, please?

what-time-is-it.meaningNote: Asking for the current time of day.
what-time-is-it.exampleSentence: Excuse me, what time is it right now?

what-day-is-today.meaningNote: Asking for the day of the week.
what-day-is-today.exampleSentence: What day is today? Is the museum open on Mondays?

what-is-todays-date.meaningNote: Asking for the calendar date (month and day).
what-is-todays-date.exampleSentence: I need to fill out this form; what is today's date?

when-does-it-open.meaningNote: Asking for the opening hour of a business, museum, or office.
when-does-it-open.exampleSentence: The door is still locked; when does it open?

when-does-it-close.meaningNote: Checking closing hours so you can plan your visit.
when-does-it-close.exampleSentence: We want to visit this evening; when does it close?

how-long-will-it-take.meaningNote: Asking for the estimated duration of a trip, wait, or service.
how-long-will-it-take.exampleSentence: How long will it take to get there by bus?

can-we-meet-tomorrow.meaningNote: Arranging an appointment or meetup for the next day.
can-we-meet-tomorrow.exampleSentence: I am busy this afternoon; can we meet tomorrow instead?

what-time-should-i-come-back.text: What time should I come back?
what-time-should-i-come-back.meaningNote: Useful when dropping off laundry, waiting for a table, or returning for a tour.
what-time-should-i-come-back.exampleSentence: I will leave my bags now; what time should I come back?

two-tickets-please.meaningNote: Useful number phrase for buying admission or transit tickets.
two-tickets-please.exampleSentence: Good morning, two tickets for the ten o'clock tour, please.

for-how-many-people.meaningNote: Common quantity question heard or asked at restaurants, tours, and hotels.
for-how-many-people.exampleSentence: We need a reservation for tonight—for how many people?

do-you-speak-english.meaningNote: Polite question before switching to English with a stranger.
do-you-speak-english.exampleSentence: Excuse me, do you speak English?

i-do-not-understand.meaningNote: Letting the speaker know you did not catch their meaning.
i-do-not-understand.exampleSentence: I am sorry, I don't understand what that means.

could-you-speak-more-slowly.meaningNote: Asking someone to slow down so you can follow along.
could-you-speak-more-slowly.exampleSentence: Could you speak more slowly, please? I am still learning.

could-you-repeat-that.meaningNote: Asking someone to say the last sentence again.
could-you-repeat-that.exampleSentence: I missed the last part; could you repeat that, please?

could-you-write-it-down.meaningNote: Helpful for addresses, prices, or unfamiliar place names.
could-you-write-it-down.exampleSentence: Could you write it down on this paper so I don't forget?

how-do-you-say-this.text: How do you say this in your language?
how-do-you-say-this.meaningNote: Useful when pointing to an object or word to learn its local name.
how-do-you-say-this.exampleSentence: How do you say this in your language?

what-does-this-mean.meaningNote: Asking for the meaning of an unfamiliar word on a sign or menu.
what-does-this-mean.exampleSentence: Excuse me, what does this word mean on the sign?

i-am-learning-your-language.meaningNote: Encourages patience and warm conversation from locals.
i-am-learning-your-language.exampleSentence: Please forgive my mistakes; I am learning your language.

please-wait-a-moment.meaningNote: Polite way to ask someone to pause while you check your bag or phone.
please-wait-a-moment.exampleSentence: Please wait a moment while I look up the address.

can-you-show-me.meaningNote: Asking someone to demonstrate or point something out directly.
can-you-show-me.exampleSentence: I am not sure how this ticket machine works; can you show me?

this-is-my-family.meaningNote: Introducing family members or showing a family photo.
this-is-my-family.exampleSentence: Hello, this is my family visiting with me.

i-am-traveling-with-my-parents.text: I am traveling with my parents.
i-am-traveling-with-my-parents.meaningNote: Explaining that you are on a trip with your mother and father.
i-am-traveling-with-my-parents.exampleSentence: I am traveling with my parents on their first trip abroad.

do-you-have-children.exampleSentence: We have two kids; do you have children?

where-is-your-family.meaningNote: Asking where someone's family is located or lives.
where-is-your-family.exampleSentence: Do they live nearby, or where is your family?

i-am-here-with-a-friend.text: I am here with a friend.
i-am-here-with-a-friend.meaningNote: Mentioning that you are visiting with a companion.
i-am-here-with-a-friend.exampleSentence: I am here with a friend from college.

this-is-my-friend.meaningNote: Used to introduce a friend to someone.
this-is-my-friend.exampleSentence: Hello, this is my friend Elena.

this-is-my-partner.meaningNote: Introducing your romantic partner or spouse.
this-is-my-partner.exampleSentence: Nice to meet you; this is my partner, Sam.

i-have-a-brother-and-a-sister.text: I have a brother and a sister.
i-have-a-brother-and-a-sister.meaningNote: Sharing how many siblings you have.
i-have-a-brother-and-a-sister.exampleSentence: I come from a small family; I have a brother and a sister.

do-you-have-brothers-or-sisters.text: Do you have brothers or sisters?
do-you-have-brothers-or-sisters.meaningNote: Asking someone if they have siblings.
do-you-have-brothers-or-sisters.exampleSentence: Do you have brothers or sisters, or are you an only child?

how-old-are-your-children.meaningNote: Friendly follow-up question when someone mentions their children.
how-old-are-your-children.exampleSentence: How old are your children now?

where-is-the-bathroom.exampleSentence: Excuse me, where is the bathroom located in this building?

how-do-i-get-to-the-station.text: How do I get to the train station?
how-do-i-get-to-the-station.meaningNote: Asking route guidance towards railway transit.
how-do-i-get-to-the-station.exampleSentence: Pardon me, how do I get to the central train station from here?

is-it-far-from-here.meaningNote: Estimating walking feasibility versus vehicle hire.
is-it-far-from-here.exampleSentence: Can we walk there, or is it far from here?

turn-left-at-the-corner.text: Turn left at the next corner
turn-left-at-the-corner.meaningNote: Navigation command directing a left turn.
turn-left-at-the-corner.exampleSentence: Walk two blocks, then turn left at the next corner.

turn-right-after-the-bank.exampleSentence: Keep going straight and turn right after the bank.

go-straight-ahead.meaningNote: Instruction to maintain the current heading without turning.
go-straight-ahead.exampleSentence: Go straight ahead until you see the cathedral.

where-am-i-on-the-map.text: Where am I on this map?
where-am-i-on-the-map.meaningNote: Asking a passerby to pinpoint your current location.
where-am-i-on-the-map.exampleSentence: I lost my orientation; where am I on this map?

is-it-within-walking-distance.meaningNote: Inquiring if a destination can be reached comfortably by foot.
is-it-within-walking-distance.exampleSentence: Is the museum within walking distance from our hotel?

where-is-the-bus-stop.text: Where is the nearest bus stop?
where-is-the-bus-stop.exampleSentence: Could you tell me where the nearest bus stop is?

i-am-lost-can-you-help.text: I am lost, can you help me?
i-am-lost-can-you-help.meaningNote: Courteous plea for navigational help when disoriented.
i-am-lost-can-you-help.exampleSentence: Excuse me, I am lost, can you help me find my hotel?

where-is-baggage-claim.text: Where is the baggage claim area?
where-is-baggage-claim.meaningNote: Inquiring about carousel location upon flight landing.
where-is-baggage-claim.exampleSentence: Our flight just landed; where is the baggage claim area?

i-have-a-hotel-reservation.text: I have a reservation under this name
i-have-a-hotel-reservation.meaningNote: Standard introduction at hotel front desk check-in.
i-have-a-hotel-reservation.exampleSentence: Good afternoon, I have a reservation under Sarah Jenkins.

what-time-is-checkout.exampleSentence: Could you tell me what time checkout is tomorrow morning?

how-much-is-a-ticket-to.text: How much is a ticket to the city center?
how-much-is-a-ticket-to.exampleSentence: Hello, how much is a one-way ticket to the city center?

which-platform-for-the-airport.text: Which platform does the airport train leave from?
which-platform-for-the-airport.meaningNote: Track or platform navigation in a rail station.
which-platform-for-the-airport.exampleSentence: Excuse me, which platform does the airport express leave from?

can-you-call-a-taxi.text: Could you call a taxi for me, please?
can-you-call-a-taxi.meaningNote: Requesting transport assistance from hotel staff or a business.
can-you-call-a-taxi.exampleSentence: I have heavy bags; could you call a taxi for me, please?

do-you-have-wifi.text: Do you have Wi-Fi here, and what is the password?
do-you-have-wifi.exampleSentence: Excuse me, do you have Wi-Fi here, and what is the password?

can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.text: Can I leave my luggage here for a few hours?
can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.meaningNote: Temporary baggage storage request before room readiness or after checkout.
can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.exampleSentence: Our flight departs late; can I leave my luggage here for a few hours?

do-you-accept-credit-cards.text: Do you accept credit cards or cash only?
do-you-accept-credit-cards.meaningNote: Clarifying payment methods before ordering goods or services.
do-you-accept-credit-cards.exampleSentence: Before we order, do you accept credit cards or cash only?

where-can-i-exchange-currency.text: Where can I safely exchange currency?
where-can-i-exchange-currency.meaningNote: Locating an authorized foreign currency exchange office.
where-can-i-exchange-currency.exampleSentence: Excuse me, where can I safely exchange foreign currency nearby?

does-this-bus-stop-here.meaningNote: Confirming that you are waiting at an active bus stop.
does-this-bus-stop-here.exampleSentence: Excuse me, does the bus to the station stop here?

where-is-the-subway-entrance.text: Where is the nearest subway station?
where-is-the-subway-entrance.meaningNote: Asking for the entrance to the underground metro system.
where-is-the-subway-entrance.exampleSentence: Excuse me, where is the nearest subway station from this plaza?

where-can-i-buy-a-transit-card.text: Where can I buy a transit card?
where-can-i-buy-a-transit-card.meaningNote: Asking where to purchase a reloadable public transit pass or ticket.
where-can-i-buy-a-transit-card.exampleSentence: Where can I buy a transit card for the bus and metro?

how-much-is-the-fare.meaningNote: Asking the driver or conductor for the ride price.
how-much-is-the-fare.exampleSentence: How much is the fare to the next stop?

which-bus-goes-to-the-city-center.text: Which bus goes to the city center?
which-bus-goes-to-the-city-center.meaningNote: Confirming the route number or bus line heading downtown.
which-bus-goes-to-the-city-center.exampleSentence: Excuse me, which bus goes to the city center from here?

does-this-train-go-to-the-airport.text: Does this train go to the airport?
does-this-train-go-to-the-airport.meaningNote: Verifying a train's destination before boarding.
does-this-train-go-to-the-airport.exampleSentence: Pardon me, does this train go to the international airport?

what-time-does-the-next-train-arrive.text: What time does the next train arrive?
what-time-does-the-next-train-arrive.meaningNote: Checking the schedule for the upcoming train.
what-time-does-the-next-train-arrive.exampleSentence: We missed the express; what time does the next train arrive?

where-should-i-get-off.meaningNote: Asking the driver or a passenger which stop is closest to your destination.
where-should-i-get-off.exampleSentence: I am going to the national museum; where should I get off?

is-this-the-right-platform.meaningNote: Confirming you are waiting on the correct track.
is-this-the-right-platform.exampleSentence: Is this the right platform for the train heading north?

please-take-me-to-this-address.text: Please take me to this address.
please-take-me-to-this-address.meaningNote: Showing a written address or map to a taxi driver.
please-take-me-to-this-address.exampleSentence: Good afternoon, please take me to this address on the card.

where-is-the-check-in-counter.meaningNote: Locating your airline's check-in desk at the airport terminal.
where-is-the-check-in-counter.exampleSentence: Excuse me, where is the check-in counter for international flights?

where-is-the-departure-gate.meaningNote: Finding the boarding gate printed on your boarding pass.
where-is-the-departure-gate.exampleSentence: Could you tell me where departure gate B12 is?

where-is-immigration.meaningNote: Locating the immigration and passport inspection hall.
where-is-immigration.exampleSentence: Excuse me, where is immigration and passport control?

here-is-my-passport.meaningNote: Spoken when handing your passport to an officer or agent.
here-is-my-passport.exampleSentence: Good morning, here is my passport and boarding pass.

i-am-here-for-tourism.meaningNote: Stating the purpose of your visit at immigration control.
i-am-here-for-tourism.exampleSentence: I am here for tourism for two weeks.

how-long-can-i-stay.meaningNote: Confirming the permitted duration of stay on your entry stamp or visa.
how-long-can-i-stay.exampleSentence: With this tourist entry stamp, how long can I stay?

i-have-nothing-to-declare.meaningNote: Standard statement at airport customs when carrying only personal items.
i-have-nothing-to-declare.exampleSentence: I only have personal clothes in my suitcase; I have nothing to declare.

my-luggage-is-missing.meaningNote: Reporting at the airport baggage service desk that your checked bag did not arrive.
my-luggage-is-missing.exampleSentence: All the bags came out on the carousel, but my luggage is missing.

is-my-flight-delayed.meaningNote: Checking with gate agents about schedule changes.
is-my-flight-delayed.exampleSentence: Excuse me, is my flight delayed or boarding on time?

could-i-have-a-window-seat.text: Could I have a window seat, please?
could-i-have-a-window-seat.meaningNote: Requesting a window seat (or aisle seat) during check-in.
could-i-have-a-window-seat.exampleSentence: If one is available, could I have a window seat, please?

can-i-check-in-early.meaningNote: Asking the hotel front desk if your room is ready before standard check-in time.
can-i-check-in-early.exampleSentence: Our flight arrived early; can I check in early today?

i-would-like-to-book-a-room.text: I would like to book a room.
i-would-like-to-book-a-room.meaningNote: Requesting a hotel room reservation for one or more nights.
i-would-like-to-book-a-room.exampleSentence: Hello, I would like to book a room for two nights.

do-you-have-any-available-rooms.text: Do you have any available rooms?
do-you-have-any-available-rooms.meaningNote: Asking about room vacancy when arriving without a booking.
do-you-have-any-available-rooms.exampleSentence: Good evening, do you have any available rooms for tonight?

i-would-like-to-check-in.text: I would like to check in, please.
i-would-like-to-check-in.meaningNote: Polite opening phrase upon arriving at your hotel reception.
i-would-like-to-check-in.exampleSentence: Good afternoon, I would like to check in, please.

i-would-like-to-check-out.text: I would like to check out, please.
i-would-like-to-check-out.meaningNote: Spoken at the hotel front desk when returning your room key and settling the bill.
i-would-like-to-check-out.exampleSentence: Good morning, I am leaving now and would like to check out, please.

what-time-is-breakfast-served.meaningNote: Asking hotel staff for morning dining hours.
what-time-is-breakfast-served.exampleSentence: What time is breakfast served in the dining room tomorrow?

is-breakfast-included.meaningNote: Checking whether morning meals are covered in the room rate.
is-breakfast-included.exampleSentence: Is breakfast included with our room reservation?

how-do-i-use-the-air-conditioning.text: How do I turn on the air conditioning?
how-do-i-use-the-air-conditioning.meaningNote: Asking hotel staff for help with the room climate controls.
how-do-i-use-the-air-conditioning.exampleSentence: Excuse me, how do I turn on the air conditioning in my room?

could-i-have-an-extra-towel.text: Could I have an extra towel, please?
could-i-have-an-extra-towel.meaningNote: Requesting fresh towels or linens from housekeeping.
could-i-have-an-extra-towel.exampleSentence: Hello, could I have an extra towel for room 302, please?

there-is-a-problem-with-my-room.text: There is a problem with my room.
there-is-a-problem-with-my-room.meaningNote: Alerting the front desk to a maintenance or plumbing issue.
there-is-a-problem-with-my-room.exampleSentence: Excuse me, there is a problem with my room; the hot water is not working.

is-there-toilet-paper.text: Excuse me, there is no toilet paper.
is-there-toilet-paper.meaningNote: Politely letting staff or an attendant know that a restroom needs paper.
is-there-toilet-paper.exampleSentence: Excuse me, there is no toilet paper in the restroom.

is-there-a-baby-changing-table.text: Is there a baby changing table?
is-there-a-baby-changing-table.meaningNote: Asking whether the restroom has facilities for infants.
is-there-a-baby-changing-table.exampleSentence: Excuse me, is there a baby changing table in this restroom?

is-there-a-public-restroom-nearby.text: Is there a public restroom nearby?
is-there-a-public-restroom-nearby.meaningNote: Asking where to find the closest public restroom while outdoors.
is-there-a-public-restroom-nearby.exampleSentence: Excuse me, is there a public restroom nearby in this park?

is-this-restroom-free.meaningNote: Checking whether a public toilet charges a small coin fee.
is-this-restroom-free.exampleSentence: Is this restroom free, or do I need coins to enter?

is-this-restroom-for-men-or-women.text: Is this restroom for men or women?
is-this-restroom-for-men-or-women.meaningNote: Clarifying unmarked or unfamiliar restroom door signs.
is-this-restroom-for-men-or-women.exampleSentence: Excuse me, is this restroom for men or women?

may-i-use-your-restroom.meaningNote: Asking a café or shop employee for permission to use the customer restroom.
may-i-use-your-restroom.exampleSentence: Excuse me, may I use your restroom, please?

is-there-a-wheelchair-accessible-restroo.meaningNote: Inquiring about step-free, accessible restroom facilities.
is-there-a-wheelchair-accessible-restroo.exampleSentence: Is there a wheelchair-accessible restroom on the ground floor?

where-can-i-wash-my-hands.text: Where can I wash my hands?
where-can-i-wash-my-hands.meaningNote: Asking for a sink or handwashing station at a restaurant or market.
where-can-i-wash-my-hands.exampleSentence: Before we eat, where can I wash my hands?

is-there-a-shower-available.meaningNote: Useful at beaches, hostels, campgrounds, and airport lounges.
is-there-a-shower-available.exampleSentence: Excuse me, is there a shower available near the beach?

where-is-a-drinking-fountain.text: Where can I find a drinking fountain?
where-is-a-drinking-fountain.meaningNote: Locating potable drinking water to refill a bottle.
where-is-a-drinking-fountain.exampleSentence: Where can I find a drinking fountain to refill my water bottle?

where-is-the-nearest-tourist-attraction.text: Where is the nearest tourist attraction?
where-is-the-nearest-tourist-attraction.meaningNote: Asking locals about notable landmarks within easy reach.
where-is-the-nearest-tourist-attraction.exampleSentence: We have a free afternoon; where is the nearest tourist attraction?

how-much-is-the-entrance-fee.text: How much is the entrance fee?
how-much-is-the-entrance-fee.meaningNote: Asking for admission prices at a museum, park, or monument.
how-much-is-the-entrance-fee.exampleSentence: Hello, how much is the entrance fee for adults?

do-i-need-to-book-in-advance.text: Do I need to book tickets in advance?
do-i-need-to-book-in-advance.meaningNote: Checking whether reservations are required before visiting an attraction.
do-i-need-to-book-in-advance.exampleSentence: Do I need to book tickets in advance, or can we buy them at the door?

is-photography-allowed.meaningNote: Checking rules before taking photos inside a museum, temple, or church.
is-photography-allowed.exampleSentence: Excuse me, is photography allowed inside the exhibition hall?

could-you-take-a-photo-of-us.text: Could you take a photo of us, please?
could-you-take-a-photo-of-us.meaningNote: Polite request when asking a passerby to take your picture at a landmark.
could-you-take-a-photo-of-us.exampleSentence: Excuse me, could you take a photo of us in front of the monument?

is-there-a-guided-tour.text: Is there a guided tour available?
is-there-a-guided-tour.meaningNote: Inquiring about scheduled tours or audio guides at a historic site.
is-there-a-guided-tour.exampleSentence: Is there a guided tour available in English this afternoon?

where-is-the-ticket-office.meaningNote: Locating the booth or counter where admission tickets are sold.
where-is-the-ticket-office.exampleSentence: Excuse me, where is the ticket office for the castle tour?

is-this-place-open-today.meaningNote: Confirming whether a museum or site is open on the current day.
is-this-place-open-today.exampleSentence: Excuse me, is this place open today or closed for the holiday?

how-long-does-the-tour-take.text: How long does the tour take?
how-long-does-the-tour-take.meaningNote: Checking the total duration of a guided visit or boat tour.
how-long-does-the-tour-take.exampleSentence: How long does the tour take from start to finish?

can-you-recommend-a-place-to-visit.text: Can you recommend a place to visit?
can-you-recommend-a-place-to-visit.meaningNote: Asking a local resident or hotel clerk for sightseeing suggestions.
can-you-recommend-a-place-to-visit.exampleSentence: We love local history; can you recommend a place to visit nearby?

where-is-the-nearest-atm.exampleSentence: Excuse me, where is the nearest ATM inside this shopping center?

do-you-have-change-for-this.text: Do you have change for this bill?
do-you-have-change-for-this.meaningNote: Asking a cashier or driver if they can break a larger banknote.
do-you-have-change-for-this.exampleSentence: I only have a large note; do you have change for this bill?

what-is-the-exchange-rate.meaningNote: Checking the currency conversion rate before exchanging money.
what-is-the-exchange-rate.exampleSentence: Good morning, what is the exchange rate for US dollars today?

can-we-split-the-bill.meaningNote: Asking a server or cashier to divide payment among companions.
can-we-split-the-bill.exampleSentence: Excuse me, can we pay separately with two cards?

my-card-is-not-working.meaningNote: Explaining that a payment terminal rejected your card so you can try another.
my-card-is-not-working.exampleSentence: My card is not working on this machine; let me try another card.

do-you-accept-cash.meaningNote: Confirming that a venue accepts banknotes and coins rather than card-only.
do-you-accept-cash.exampleSentence: Do you accept cash here, or is it digital payment only?

can-i-pay-with-my-phone.text: Can I pay using my phone?
can-i-pay-with-my-phone.meaningNote: Asking whether contactless mobile wallets or QR payments are accepted.
can-i-pay-with-my-phone.exampleSentence: Can I pay using my phone at this register?

could-i-have-a-receipt.text: Could I have a receipt, please?
could-i-have-a-receipt.exampleSentence: Thank you, could I have a receipt for this purchase, please?

i-think-i-was-charged-twice.text: I think I was charged twice.
i-think-i-was-charged-twice.meaningNote: Politely pointing out a duplicate charge on a bill or card receipt.
i-think-i-was-charged-twice.exampleSentence: Excuse me, could you check the bill? I think I was charged twice.

is-there-an-additional-fee.meaningNote: Checking for extra service charges, taxes, or ATM withdrawal fees.
is-there-an-additional-fee.exampleSentence: Before we confirm, is there an additional fee for paying by card?

what-is-the-weather-like.meaningNote: Everyday question about current outdoor conditions.
what-is-the-weather-like.exampleSentence: Have you been outside yet? What's the weather like today?

is-it-going-to-rain.meaningNote: Checking if rain is expected before heading out.
is-it-going-to-rain.exampleSentence: The sky looks dark; is it going to rain this afternoon?

it-is-very-hot-today.meaningNote: Commenting on warm or humid weather.
it-is-very-hot-today.exampleSentence: It's very hot today; let's sit in the shade.

is-there-a-storm-coming.meaningNote: Asking locals about approaching severe weather.
is-there-a-storm-coming.exampleSentence: The wind is picking up; is there a storm coming?

should-i-bring-an-umbrella.meaningNote: Asking advice on whether rain gear is needed.
should-i-bring-an-umbrella.exampleSentence: We are walking to the market; should I bring an umbrella?

what-is-the-weather-forecast.text: What is the weather forecast for tomorrow?
what-is-the-weather-forecast.meaningNote: Checking next-day weather conditions to plan outdoor activities.
what-is-the-weather-forecast.exampleSentence: We want to hike early; what is the weather forecast for tomorrow?

it-is-very-cold-today.exampleSentence: It is very cold today compared to yesterday.

is-the-air-quality-okay.text: Is the air quality okay today?
is-the-air-quality-okay.meaningNote: Checking for haze, smoke, or pollution levels before outdoor exercise.
is-the-air-quality-okay.exampleSentence: It looks a little hazy; is the air quality okay today?

is-it-going-to-be-sunny-tomorrow.text: Is it going to be sunny tomorrow?
is-it-going-to-be-sunny-tomorrow.meaningNote: Checking if clear skies are expected the next day.
is-it-going-to-be-sunny-tomorrow.exampleSentence: We planned a beach trip; is it going to be sunny tomorrow?

do-i-need-a-jacket.meaningNote: Asking if the evening or destination will be cool enough to need outerwear.
do-i-need-a-jacket.exampleSentence: Does it get cool at night here, or do I need a jacket?

help-me-please.text: Please help me! / I need help
help-me-please.meaningNote: Urgent, universal cry for immediate assistance in distress.
help-me-please.exampleSentence: Please help me, somebody grabbed my backpack!

call-an-ambulance.meaningNote: Direct medical emergency instruction to bystanders.
call-an-ambulance.exampleSentence: Someone collapsed; please call an ambulance immediately!

call-the-police.meaningNote: Instruction to contact law enforcement immediately.
call-the-police.exampleSentence: There has been a break-in; please call the police right now!

where-is-the-nearest-hospital.text: Where is the nearest hospital or clinic?
where-is-the-nearest-hospital.exampleSentence: My companion has severe abdominal pain; where is the nearest hospital?

i-need-a-doctor.text: I need to see a doctor who speaks English
i-need-a-doctor.meaningNote: Requesting a bilingual physician to guarantee clear clinical diagnosis.
i-need-a-doctor.exampleSentence: I feel unwell and need to see a doctor who speaks English.

where-is-a-pharmacy.text: Where is the nearest open pharmacy?
where-is-a-pharmacy.exampleSentence: I have a headache; where is the nearest open pharmacy?

i-lost-my-passport.text: I lost my passport and wallet
i-lost-my-passport.meaningNote: Reporting missing legal identification and funds to authorities.
i-lost-my-passport.exampleSentence: I need help reaching my embassy because I lost my passport.

i-cannot-breathe.meaningNote: Critical indicator of asthma, allergic anaphylaxis, or cardiac issues.
i-cannot-breathe.exampleSentence: Please sit me up and assist me, I am having trouble breathing.

there-is-a-fire.text: There is a fire, evacuate the building!
there-is-a-fire.meaningNote: Urgent hazard warning to prompt building evacuation.
there-is-a-fire.exampleSentence: I smell thick smoke; there is a fire, evacuate the building!

where-is-the-nearest-police-station.text: Where is the nearest police station?
where-is-the-nearest-police-station.meaningNote: Direct question to locate the closest police station.
where-is-the-nearest-police-station.exampleSentence: Excuse me, where is the nearest police station?

what-is-the-emergency-number.text: What is the emergency phone number?
what-is-the-emergency-number.meaningNote: Asking for the local emergency telephone number.
what-is-the-emergency-number.exampleSentence: What is the emergency phone number in this country?

please-leave-me-alone.meaningNote: Firm, clear statement asking someone to step away.
please-leave-me-alone.exampleSentence: Please leave me alone right now.

someone-stole-my-belongings.exampleSentence: I need to speak to an officer; someone stole my belongings.

i-need-a-police-report.text: I need a copy of the police report.
i-need-a-police-report.meaningNote: Requesting an official written report at a police station.
i-need-a-police-report.exampleSentence: I need a copy of the police report for my records.

my-wallet-was-stolen.meaningNote: Reporting that your wallet was taken.
my-wallet-was-stolen.exampleSentence: My wallet was stolen on the crowded bus.

i-have-been-robbed.meaningNote: Direct statement reporting a robbery to police or staff.
i-have-been-robbed.exampleSentence: Please help me call the police; I have been robbed.

i-do-not-feel-safe-here.meaningNote: Expressing concern about personal safety in a location.
i-do-not-feel-safe-here.exampleSentence: I don't feel safe here; let's go inside the hotel.

i-need-to-report-an-incident.text: I need to report an incident.
i-need-to-report-an-incident.meaningNote: Spoken at a police desk to file an official statement.
i-need-to-report-an-incident.exampleSentence: Good afternoon, I need to report an incident that just happened.

help-me-contact-the-embassy.text: Can you help me contact my embassy?
help-me-contact-the-embassy.meaningNote: Asking for assistance reaching your country's embassy or consulate.
help-me-contact-the-embassy.exampleSentence: Can you help me contact my embassy by phone?

do-i-need-a-prescription.text: Do I need a prescription for this medicine?
do-i-need-a-prescription.meaningNote: Asking a pharmacist whether a doctor's prescription is required.
do-i-need-a-prescription.exampleSentence: Excuse me, do I need a prescription for this medicine?

how-often-should-i-take-this-medicine.text: How often should I take this medicine?
how-often-should-i-take-this-medicine.meaningNote: Asking a doctor or pharmacist to clarify the dosage schedule.
how-often-should-i-take-this-medicine.exampleSentence: How often should I take this medicine each day?

i-have-travel-insurance.meaningNote: Informing hospital or clinic reception that you carry travel insurance.
i-have-travel-insurance.exampleSentence: Here is my policy card; I have travel health insurance.

i-do-not-feel-well.meaningNote: General statement letting others know you are feeling ill.
i-do-not-feel-well.exampleSentence: I need to rest for a moment; I don't feel well.

i-have-a-headache.meaningNote: Describing head pain to a doctor or pharmacist.
i-have-a-headache.exampleSentence: I have had a headache since this morning.

i-have-a-fever.exampleSentence: I feel chills and I think I have a fever.

i-have-stomach-pain.exampleSentence: I need to see a doctor because I have stomach pain.

i-am-allergic-to-this-medicine.text: I am allergic to this medicine.
i-am-allergic-to-this-medicine.meaningNote: Informing medical or pharmacy staff of a medication allergy.
i-am-allergic-to-this-medicine.exampleSentence: Please check the chart; I am allergic to this medicine.

do-you-have-pain-relievers.meaningNote: Asking a pharmacist for pain relief medication.
do-you-have-pain-relievers.exampleSentence: Excuse me, do you have pain relievers at this counter?

i-need-medical-assistance.meaningNote: Clear request for professional medical care.
i-need-medical-assistance.exampleSentence: Please help me, I need medical assistance right away.

i-lost-my-bag.meaningNote: Reporting a missing bag to staff or transit personnel.
i-lost-my-bag.exampleSentence: Excuse me, I lost my bag a few minutes ago.

has-anyone-found-my-phone.meaningNote: Asking staff if a missing mobile phone was turned in.
has-anyone-found-my-phone.exampleSentence: I was sitting at that table; has anyone found my phone?

where-is-the-lost-and-found-office.text: Where is the lost and found office?
where-is-the-lost-and-found-office.meaningNote: Locating the office where recovered items are kept.
where-is-the-lost-and-found-office.exampleSentence: Excuse me, where is the lost and found office in this station?

i-left-something-here.meaningNote: Explaining when returning to a shop or restaurant to look for a forgotten item.
i-left-something-here.exampleSentence: Hello, I was here ten minutes ago and I left something here.

i-cannot-find-my-belongings.meaningNote: Reporting that your personal items are missing.
i-cannot-find-my-belongings.exampleSentence: I checked my locker, and I can't find my belongings.

i-lost-my-keys.meaningNote: Reporting missing room or personal keys.
i-lost-my-keys.exampleSentence: Excuse me, I lost my keys somewhere in the lobby.

i-left-my-bag-on-the-train.text: I left my bag on the train.
i-left-my-bag-on-the-train.meaningNote: Reporting an item accidentally left aboard a train.
i-left-my-bag-on-the-train.exampleSentence: Excuse me, I just got off and I left my bag on the train.

please-call-me-if-you-find-it.text: Please call me if you find it.
please-call-me-if-you-find-it.meaningNote: Spoken when leaving your phone number with staff.
please-call-me-if-you-find-it.exampleSentence: Here is my phone number; please call me if you find it.

can-i-describe-it-to-you.text: Can I describe it to you?
can-i-describe-it-to-you.meaningNote: Offering details of a lost item's color, brand, or size.
can-i-describe-it-to-you.exampleSentence: It is a small black backpack; can I describe it to you?

can-i-fill-out-a-form.text: Can I fill out a form?
can-i-fill-out-a-form.meaningNote: Asking to complete a written lost-property claim form.
can-i-fill-out-a-form.exampleSentence: Can I fill out a form with my contact details?

i-feel-very-dizzy.text: I feel very dizzy and weak
i-feel-very-dizzy.exampleSentence: I need to sit down immediately; I feel very dizzy and weak.
